reasoning_traces.think:
The core operator is a deep regression network that transforms 3D marker trajectories into knee joint moments using spatio-temporal image encoding. The CNN architecture encodes motion capture data into 227×227 RGB images, which are processed through a pre-trained CaffeNet backbone modified with a Euclidean loss layer for multi-output regression. This allows direct estimation of six components of 3D knee joint moments (KJM) without inverse dynamics. Transfer learning is applied in a double-cascade manner: first from ImageNet, then from a GRF/M model, to adapt high-level visual features to biomechanical signals. The system focuses on the initial 33% of the stance phase, where injury risk is most pronounced. The output is compressed using PCA to reduce redundancy while preserving variance. This framework enables real-time monitoring of on-field workload exposure and injury risk. Failure modes include marker occlusion, motion variability outside training domain, and misalignment between image encoding and biomechanical signal structure.
